{
  "research_question": "Does the stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a One-Way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the fixed factor to test the omnibus null hypothesis that all group means are equal.",
    "For 'Success' (binary, 0/1), acknowledge that the distribution is Bernoulli and technically violates ANOVA normality assumptions; however, given the large sample size (n=76655) and expected central limit theorem effects, proceed with ANOVA as an approximation, but flag it for potential transformation (e.g., arcsine) or replacement with logistic regression if diagnostic checks fail.",
    "Test the omnibus F-statistic for each variable at alpha=0.05. If p < 0.05, reject the null hypothesis and proceed to post-hoc analysis."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality of residuals: Check Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests on residuals for each variable within each paradigm group. 'Time-to-Target' and 'AD' may require checking for skew given their ranges (0.5-201.39 and 0.0006-1.0 respectively).",
    "Homogeneity of Variances: Perform Levene's or Bartlett's test across the five groups for each response variable. 'Path Efficiency' shows a wide range (0.0009-29.8) which suggests potential heteroscedasticity requiring Welch's ANOVA or data transformation.",
    "Independence of observations: Verify the 'Mouse' column (8 levels, ~10,000 per level) ensures subjects are not nested in a way that violates independence (i.e., one mouse per trial or accounting for repeated measures if applicable, though the summary implies a pooled dataset).",
    "Homogeneity of variance is critical for 'AD' and 'Average Speed' given the different mins/maxs across variables."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If any omnibus ANOVA result is significant (p < 0.05), conduct a Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) test to identify which specific pairs of stimulation paradigms differ significantly.",
    "Adjust for multiple comparisons across the five response variables using the Bonferroni correction (alpha_new = 0.05 / 5 = 0.01) to control the Family-Wise Error Rate.",
    "Report mean differences and 95% confidence intervals for significant pairwise comparisons."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows superior performance (lower Time-to-Target, higher Success, higher Path Efficiency, higher Average Speed, lower AD) compared to Sham, as it includes all modalities.",
    "ICMS Only may show intermediate performance compared to visual-only conditions, depending on the specific neural pathways targeted.",
    "Visual-only conditions (Dim vs Bright) may differ significantly in 'Time-to-Target' and 'AD', with 'Bright Visual Only' potentially outperforming 'Dim Visual Only' due to better stimulus visibility.",
    "Success rates may be highest in 'Combined' and lowest in 'Sham' if the tasks require active intervention beyond passive observation."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The 'Success' variable is binary (0/1); standard ANOVA assumes continuous, normally distributed data. While the large N mitigates this, a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with binomial distribution would be statistically more rigorous.",
    "Large variance in 'Path Efficiency' (min ~0 to max ~30) suggests potential outliers or mixing of very inefficient and highly efficient paths, violating homogeneity of variance assumptions.",
    "The dataset summary does not explicitly state if 'Mouse' is a random effect; if multiple trials per mouse exist, a mixed-effects model is required rather than a standard one-way ANOVA.",
    "Missingness is reported as 0, but the filtering process excluded 2012 rows, potentially introducing selection bias if the excluded data was non-random."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a Mixed-Effects Model (Linear Mixed Model) with 'Stim Paradigm' as a fixed effect and 'Mouse' as a random intercept to account for potential repeated measures, alongside a Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM) with a binomial link function for the 'Success' variable."
}
